question: Sussex, 1912. A gravel pit yields a human-looking skull and an ape-like jaw. What was Piltdown Man?
answer: A forgery: a human skull and an orangutan's jaw, stained to look ancient. It fooled experts for 40 years because it showed what many hoped to see: a big brain first, and in England. Every real fossil found later showed the reverse order, apelike brains with humanlike teeth, and Piltdown fitted none of them.
move: Be most suspicious of the evidence that flatters what you hoped.
ask: Which finding did I accept fastest because it was exactly what I wanted?

clues.text: Skull and jaw lie in old gravel beside bones of long-extinct animals.
The parts that would prove jaw and skull fit together are broken off.
1949: the bones hold almost no fluorine, which buried bone soaks up over ages.
1953, under a microscope: fine scratches on the molars. They were filed flat.
The jaw is an orangutan's, stained brown to match the gravel.

scene.why: Fluorine made the bones young; the file marks made them deliberate. Nature doesn't file teeth.

reference: Weiner, Oakley & Le Gros Clark, The solution of the Piltdown problem, Bulletin of the British Museum (Natural History), Geology 2(3):141-146, 1953
